Element.attribute: MAR 2017 - included optional inputs with other inputs|NOV 2015 - changed output to newly created outcome

Configure the package application according to configuration parameters for the business environment or function. This typically includes the metadata and data structures the application will operate in, like a chart of accounts, legal entities, organizational structure or reporting dimensional hierarchy. Configure basic solution functionality for each of the functional teams so basic processes can be tested. Refer to guidance documents for any package specific considerations.

This is the starting point to allow testing to begin. Some details of configuration settings may not be known at this time, but the basic configuration can be completed.

The purpose of this task is to:

  • Customize the package application with the specific configuration settings for the functional processes
  • Implement the core configuration, write valid test cases and document in solution-specific management tools as required
  • Allow basic testing to start
  • Allow for more specific design details to be fleshed out

Element.Name: Unit test configuration
Element.copyright:
© 2012, 2022 EYGM Limited. All Rights Reserved.
Privacy Notice

Powered by Global Methods in conjunction with Consulting Methods
Element.attribute:
1. Write unit test scripts

Develop unit test scripts based on functional requirements, including expected outcomes in the script. Unit test scripts form the building blocks to create assembly, integration and user acceptance tests, therefore test scripts should be detailed and robust so they can used by the test workstream to develop other tests.

2. Define unit test data

Define required data elements for successful unit testing of either the code or configured object. For the purpose of unit testing, the data needed will be created.

3. Review and sign off unit test scripts

Review unit test scripts with the test workstream and functional teams (including key client stakeholders). Obtain sign-off from these parties before proceeding.

4. Perform unit tests and log results

Execute unit test according to approved test scripts and record results, including whether expected (and desired) results were achieved. Screenshots and key output should be attached to the test and form documentation to support approval of test results by the test workstream.

5. Fix defects and retest

Resolve defects (i.e., configuration changes or code fixes) and retest. Record test results including whether the object produced the expected (and desired) result. Repeat tasks 4 and 5 until all major defects have been resolved.
